376082142.assessment: The original screen positive is smooth double-wave modulation, rather than an established discrete eclipse. Three QLP sector folds and four-harmonic residual diagnostics show no narrow residual recurring at the searched phase. This refutes the proposed eclipsing morphology at the measured signal; shallow additional eclipses are not excluded.
376082142.source: Fresh cutouts were obtained, but no eclipsing deficit is established to localize. Morphology is the deciding failure, not a missing pixel test. The smooth variable itself has not been assigned a by-catch host.
376082142.geometry: The doubled BLS interval follows the Gaia orbit approximately, but a modulation period is not an eclipse-derived period. No eclipse conjunction geometry is claimed.
376082142.limitations: No established eclipse; the smooth signal could be ellipsoidal or other variability. Harmonics can absorb broad events and do not prove absence of shallow eclipses.
376082142.next_check: Search higher precision data for a discrete narrow eclipse only if this smooth variable remains of interest.

285942031.assessment: Deep, repeated discrete eclipses are real and source fits favor the target in two detector sectors. The Gaia orbit has material timing tension, so the geometry check is not fully passed.
285942031.source: Signed difference images, Gaussian free-center diagnostics and fixed-coordinate target-versus-neighbour fits are preserved in raw-evidence. The fixed-position neighbour/target residual sums of squares consistently favor the target. Ratios are descriptive, not formal significance; source PRF mismatch is a limitation.
285942031.geometry: Photometric period 2.606854146 d versus Gaia 2.607369245 ± 0.00013636 d; difference -3.78 Gaia sigma. Nearest approximate conjunction A: offset -0.355 d; linear covariance error 0.074 d, conservative sum bound 0.342 d. Observed median duration 3.74 h versus approximate central feasibility 5.47 h. Phase uncertainty and approximate geometry are retained rather than treating a linear sigma as exact.
285942031.limitations: Gaia period differs by -3.78 sigma; approximate conjunction is 0.355 d off versus linear covariance error 0.074 d. The conservative sum error is 0.342 d; a nonlinear orbital posterior or fresh RV fit is needed before treating this as the Gaia eclipsing system.
285942031.next_check: Reassess Gaia orbital uncertainties/correlations or obtain an updated radial-velocity orbit to resolve the eclipse-versus-Gaia timing tension.

126363604.assessment: Four sharp repeat eclipses are visible over a variable stellar baseline; all four centers define an eclipse period. Raw-event scatter is inflated by variability, so the initial depth/RMS gate was explicitly relaxed after fold inspection. Fresh imaging supports the target but does not fully exclude its closest capable source.
126363604.source: Four individual signed difference images in sectors7,61,88 place fitted deficits3.93,1.34,0.81,0.82 arcsec from the target. Nearest capable neighbour is11.14 arcsec. The first-sector fixed-source residual ratio is only1.78; repeat source positions support the target but the PSF systematics are uncalibrated. Custom extraction recovers repeated deficits in the same TESS photons.
126363604.geometry: Photometric period 16.505959732 d versus Gaia 16.499031114 ± 0.00363290 d; difference 1.91 Gaia sigma. Nearest approximate conjunction B: offset 0.657 d; linear covariance error 0.290 d, conservative sum bound 1.352 d. Observed median duration 8.22 h versus approximate central feasibility 22.88 h. Phase uncertainty and approximate geometry are retained rather than treating a linear sigma as exact.
126363604.limitations: Closest capable host not conclusively excluded under the source model; approximate Gaia conjunction offset0.657 d has linear covariance error0.290 d, with broad conservative uncertainty. Stellar variability affects local timing/depth.
126363604.next_check: Validate the repeated difference-image astrometry with a multi-source PRF or higher resolution event photometry; refine Gaia conjunction uncertainty if needed.
